name: 4EverAble2Shell
tile_line: Exploited, no login. Axis bug in KEV, due 21 Nov.
tldr: 4EverAble2Shell gives attackers root on on-prem N-able N-central servers with the Legacy API on, no login needed. Exploit public, attacks seen, its Axis bug is on CISA's exploited list. Patch now to 2026.4 HF3 or later; until then, turn off the Legacy API.
summary: A public exploit chain gives an attacker root on on-prem N-central servers that have the old Legacy API turned on, with no login. It gets in through an Apache Axis bug (CVE-2026-90436); the N-central root step has no CVE yet. Security firm Huntback found crypto miners on 21 servers within hours, and N-able reported attacks on 13 Nov.

affected.label: On-prem N-central below 2026.4 HF3
affected.text: Hotfix 2 (2026.4.1.26, 10 Nov) does not stop this chain; the exploit was tested on it. Hotfix 3 (2026.4.1.39, 16 Nov) removes the Legacy API. N-able says hosted N-central is not vulnerable to the server chain and gets HF3 automatically.

affected.label: Legacy API is enabled
affected.text: Off by default, but admins can turn it on under Administration > Mail and Network Settings > Network Security > LEGACY APIS. N-able and the researcher agree the server chain needs it on and reachable.

affected.label: Attacker can reach the server
affected.text: No login needed: the Axis bug fires while the SOAP request is parsed, before any per-service auth runs. N-able says the server chain needs the Legacy API enabled and exposed to the internet.

do.label: Upgrade to 2026.4 HF3 (2026.4.1.39)
do.text: Rapid7 says apply it as an emergency, outside normal patch cycles. HF3 permanently blocks the Legacy API and fixes 17 new CVEs. Also update all Agents and Probes to 2026.4.1 HF3, and Patch Management Engine to 2.14.4.5829 or later.

do.label: Until then: turn off Legacy API
do.text: Make sure the LEGACY APIS setting is off, even on HF2. If you truly need it, never expose it to the internet.

do.label: Hunt for compromise
do.text: Look in web logs for requests to `/dms/services/ServerUI` that mention `jline.internal.TerminalLineSettings`, an unexpected `xvd.service` unit, mining processes, files in `/tmp/.xvd` or `/var/tmp/.xvd`, and traffic to 157.20.241[.]16. If found, treat the server as fully owned (root).

do.label: Then clean up downstream
do.text: A hacked RMM server reaches every managed client. Rotate secrets stored in Automation Manager policies, enforce MFA on N-central accounts, and review activity from 11 Nov on for new accounts, scripts, scheduled tasks and remote sessions. The same Axis bug was also exploited against Confluence Data Center on 13 Nov.

slack: 4EverAble2Shell (N-able N-central): public exploit chain gives unauthenticated root on on-prem N-central servers with Legacy API enabled. It uses Apache Axis CVE-2026-90436 (CISA KEV, added 18 Nov, due 21 Nov). Huntback found miners on 21 servers within hours (most on Hotfix 2); N-able reported attacks on 13 Nov. Fix: upgrade the server to 2026.4 HF3 (2026.4.1.39), which removes the Legacy API, and update Agents and Probes. Until then, make sure Legacy API is off, and check for xvd.service or /tmp/.xvd. Hosted N-central: N-able says not vulnerable.
